title: Stowaway prefill fieldnotes
content:
Week: 2027-06-07 -> 2027-06-13
Owners: Aisha (prefill lead), Miguel (kernel), Priya (kv-cache/eviction), Evan (ops handoff)
Attendees: Aisha, Miguel, Priya, Evan, Sasha (oncall), Tom (bench) — ad-hoc: Riya stopped by for 20m

Purpose
- Capture observational notes from the small experiment we ran to shadow prefill traffic on the stowaway path (low-priority cohort). This doc is intentionally informal — action items and triage notes below.

Summary / high level
- Stowaway prefill successfully shadowed ~4% of live traffic to a separate prefill allocator without impacting primary routing latency (p99 change < 2ms).
- Kernel handshake changes (microbatch RSVP) introduced a sporadic 20ms tail on sequences >1k tokens in synthetic bench; we saw no customer regressions in production traffic but need root cause.
- KV-cache eviction pressure climbed in the late-afternoon window when cohort arrival spikes overlapped with bursty long-context jobs. Some slot churn observed (see metrics).

What we ran
- Shadow pipeline enabled for cohort id: stowaway-45 between 09:00-18:00 PDT on 2027-06-10.
- Prefill allocator limited to 1/8th of a node to force evictions and reveal edge cases.
- Kernel build: microbatch-rsvp-v3 (PR 2198) with debug flags on for handshake timings.
- Sampling: 1 in 1000 full requests included heavy long-context (>2048 tokens) workload to stress KV path.

Observed metrics (selected)
- Prefetch hit rate: 72% steady; dip to 58% during a 20m spike (16:05-16:25).
- KV eviction rate: baseline 0.3 evicts/min -> spike to 2.8 evicts/min during dip window.
- p50 end-to-end latency (stowaway shadow): 38ms; p99: 226ms (with microbatch RSVP off p99 was ~210ms).
- Kernel handshake tail: ~0.3% of handshakes measured >40ms; correlated with GC cycles in the node that had slightly older CUDA driver.

Immediate takeaways
- Driver mismatch hypothesis: one of the test nodes had an older CUDA stack; upgrading that image removed the 20ms tail in local repros. Action: bump node images in stowaway pool to cuda-12.3-optimized by EOD 2027-06-15. (owner: Miguel)
- Eviction cliff: combined effect of intentionally throttled prefill allocator and a burst of long-context jobs. Short-term mitigation: raise prefill allocator cap from 1/8 -> 1/6 nodes during the 15:00-18:00 window for stowaway cohort; schedule via autoscale policy override (owner: Evan).
- Prefetch heuristics: 72% hit rate is promising, but dip patterns show that prefix length and token distribution from that cohort are brittle. We should add a short TTL bump for prefixes with >512 tokens (owner: Priya) for 48 hours of testing.

Decisions made
- Keep shadowing for two more full business days to validate that driver bump + cap change removes tails and stabilizes eviction rate.
- Gate merging of microbatch-rsvp-v3 until kernel handshake repro is stable on upgraded image and no regression in nightly bench. PR 2198 to remain open but feature-flagged.

Open questions / things to investigate
- Why did only one node show the handshake tail despite identical image tags? Hypothesis: late / incomplete rollout of driver on ephemeral nodes; need a node bootstrap audit (JIRA-RW-7620).
- Is prefix TTL bump masking underlying cache fragmentation? If so, we might be delaying failures rather than fixing root cause. Long-term: dataset of prefix reuse ratios by model/route (owner: Priya / data-ops).
- Could microbatch handshake ordering be sensitive to arrival-time jitter causing head-of-line interactions? Add instrumentation to kernel to correlate arrival jitter with handshake times (owner: Miguel).

Action items (short)
- Miguel: rollout node image bump to stowaway pool and run handshake microbench on 50-node sample — due 2027-06-15.
- Evan: temporary autoscale policy override for stowaway 15:00-18:00 window to 1/6 nodes — due 2027-06-15.
- Priya: implement and toggle short TTL bump (+15s) for prefixes >512 tokens for cohort risk testing — due 2027-06-16.
- Aisha: schedule post-shadow sync Friday 2027-06-18 10:00 PDT, write up short experiment README and link to PR/bench results.
- Tom: run end-to-end bench including long-context synthetic jobs with microbatch RSVP on/off and produce CSV for p50/p95/p99 — due 2027-06-16.

Notes from the sync (freeform)
- Sasha: Oncall had 2 paged incidents unrelated to this experiment (network flaps in us-west2), flagged but did not correlate. We should still exclude those time windows from analysis.
- Riya: suggested a small dark-launch where we replay recorded sequences against prefill path to test eviction without exposing request variation. Good idea, create RW ticket.
- Conversation: we debated TTL bump magnitude (15s vs 60s). Decided to start small (15s) to avoid warmup spike.

Risks / mitigation
- Risk: TTL bump could increase memory pressure causing more evictions on larger cohorts. Mitigation: only enable for stowaway and monitor evict rate; rapid rollback plan exists.
- Risk: kernel changes may interact with some older model variants that do manual caching. Mitigation: feature-flag microbatch RSVP per model family and do small canary.

Longer-term follow-ups
- Metric: build a dashboard that cross-correlates handshake tail, driver version, and node boot time for easier triage. (owner: Miguel + Observability)
- Research: evaluate alternate eviction policy that prefers retaining longer prefixes when hit-rate delta >10% (owner: Priya + Applied-ML).
- Design: spec for a prefill admission controller that can make admission decisions based on active KV pressure and estimated reuse score. Draft: RW-7901.

Appendix: quick logs and references
- Minimal reproducer: bench script stowaway/repro/handshake_tail.sh (linked in PR 2198).
- Quick grep of kernel logs: /var/log/serving-runtime/handshake-debug-20270610.log (rotated).
- Important tickets: JIRA-RW-7562 (stowaway experiment), JIRA-RW-7620 (node bootstrap audit), JIRA-RW-7901 (prefill admission controller).

Next sync: Friday 2027-06-18 10:00 PDT, 30m. Agenda: results after image bump + autoscale override, TTL bump observed effects, decide on safe merge window for microbatch RSVP.

Notes to self
- Keep this doc short; write a cleaned-up version in Confluence if we want to preserve decisions.
- If we see any customer-facing regressions, escalate to product immediately and flip feature flag.
